walkthroughs.body_html:
If God is all-powerful and all-loving, why is there evil?

Epicurus' challenge: God is either unable, unwilling, or doesn't exist.

Moral evil (human-caused) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease) both demand an answer.

A theodicy tries to defend God's goodness.

Augustine: evil came from human sin (the Fall) — it is the absence of good, not a thing God made.

Irenaeus: God made us imperfect on purpose so we can grow toward him. Suffering builds the soul.

Free-will defence: love must be chosen — and choice means evil is possible.

Atheism denies God exists. Agnosticism says we can't know.

Reasons people don't believe today:

1. The problem of evil — too much suffering.
2. Science seems to explain the world (Big Bang, evolution) without God.
3. Upbringing — fewer people raised religious.
4. Bad behaviour by religious people puts them off.
Believers reply: science answers 'how', religion answers 'why'.
